title: Education collocations
instructions: Choose the word that forms the strongest natural collocation.
author: QEVRANT editorial (AI-assisted draft)

questions.prompt: Only half the class managed to ___ the deadline.
Over 600 candidates will ___ the exam on Saturday. (British English)
questions.explanation: In British English you **sit** or **take** an exam. *Give an exam* is what an examiner does in some varieties, not a candidate.

questions.prompt: The team ___ research in twelve schools.
questions.explanation: **Conduct**, **carry out** or **do** research. *Make research* is a common error.

questions.prompt: You'll need a good ___ of statistics for this module.
questions.explanation: **a good / firm grasp of** something = a good understanding of it.
**stifle** creativity / innovation / debate = stop it developing.

questions.prompt: Group projects are designed to ___ independence and cooperation.
questions.explanation: **foster** = encourage something to develop (formal). *Rise* is intransitive and *grow up* is used for people.

questions.prompt: If you miss two seminars, it's easy to fall ___ with the reading.
questions.explanation: **fall behind (with)** = fail to keep up. *Fall back* means retreat; *fall out* means argue.

questions.prompt: She ___ back from a terrible first year and graduated with distinction.
questions.explanation: **bounce back (from)** = recover after a difficult period.

questions.prompt: Weekly quizzes work as ___ assessment: they count for nothing but show you what to revise.
questions.explanation: **formative assessment** gives feedback during learning; **summative assessment** gives a final grade.

questions.prompt: The report links low educational ___ to a shortage of specialist teachers.
questions.explanation: **educational attainment** and **the attainment gap** are fixed academic collocations.
